title: Learning piano by ear, Maple Leaf Rag, and starting in vaudeville
summary: He picked up piano from watching a cousin, learned Maple Leaf Rag by ear from a fellow, and went on the Orpheum circuit about 1912-13 with Guy McCormick and Fitzgerald. He never read music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And I wanted to ask you some things about your piano playing and composing. How did you get started?

Well, it's a strange thing. I used to have, my mother raised her niece years ago and she played a little piano. And I used to fool around watching her, you know. And I finally got to it and I played chopsticks, you know, those little things. I used to have to play with my mother. But it was the strangest thing in the world. When I learned how to play piano, it was a fellow, I can't think of his name. But I think it was Maple Leaf Rag or something like that. He taught me. And gee, that's the most difficult thing in the world. And you know that's one of the first numbers I played? Oh, really? Isn't that something? By ear? Yeah, just by ear. Just watching him, you know, and listening to him. And that's how I started and I kept on going. And then got in the audible in 1912, I think it was, something like that, 12 or 13, with Guy McCormick and a fellow by the name of Fitzgerald out of Chicago. And we played the off-room circuit. We were out about two or three years. And I came back here and I played in the cafes. That's about all I can remember now, I guess.
Yeah, well, I'll refresh your memory. Okay, a little bit. Did you ever get any piano teaching at all?

Oh, no. I wouldn't know. I don't know one note from another. Yeah, look at this. I wouldn't know. It was mine if it didn't have my name on. I wouldn't know. No, I don't know one note from the other. Isn't that strange?
